channel.description: Latest articles from Small Wars Journal (smallwarsjournal.com)

item.title: Dragos Documents First LLM-Assisted Strike on Water Infrastructure in Mexico
item.description: Check out what a recent AI-assisted cyberattack on Mexican water utilities reveals about weak infrastructure and governance across Latin America.

item.title: Part 2: The U.S. Munitions Problem
item.description: The U.S. fired over 1,000 Tomahawks in 39 days. Resupply takes four years. Here's what that means for the next war.

item.title: The Insurance Weapon: How Commercial Risk Logic Became an Irregular Warfare Tool at Hormuz
item.description: Insurance markets closed Hormuz before force did—war risk repricing triggered a self-enforcing maritime shutdown, redefining irregular warfare at chokepoints.

item.title: AI-First Professional Military Education: Validating the Grade Chain Before the Kill Chain
item.description: PME can rigorously test AI-augmented decision-making and train leaders to critically interrogate AI recommendations.

item.title: The Steppe Is Not a Fortress: What Mongolia Can Learn from Iran’s Mosaic Defense
item.description: This article analyzes the ways in which the decentralization of Iran's "mosaic defense" system could serve as an example for Mongolia.

item.title: Russia's Spring Offensive Begins Against Ukraine’s Fortress Belt: ISW
item.description: Russian forces have launched a multi-axis offensive against Ukraine’s Fortress Belt, combining dispersed assaults, drone strikes, and air interdiction, while facing high casualties and Ukrainian countermeasures.

item.title: The Rise of Non-State Special Operations | The War Room Podcast
item.description: How non-state groups conduct elite-style operations. Craig Whiteside joins War Room to explore strategy, risk, and modern threats.

item.title: Communicative Deterrence in the Information Environment | Irregular Warfare Center
item.description: Dr. Rupinder Mangat explains communicative deterrence and how resilience in the information environment helps counter adversarial influence operations.

item.title: Combat Debut of the Precision Strike Missile (PrSM): Implications
item.description: The Precision Strike Missile proves its combat value in Iran, highlighting its role in long-range strike operations and the urgent need to expand U.S. production and stockpiles.

item.title: March to the Sound of the Guns: Organizational Integration for Strategic Competition
item.description: Place information warfare professionals where the fight is during strategic competition to better achieve national objectives short of war.

item.title: Easier to Kill Than to Text: A Mandate for Information Warfare Reform
item.description: In an era of relentless narrative warfare, this article calls for a new American way of war—realigning talent and doctrine to integrate information, military, diplomatic, and economic power for strategic advantage.

item.title: The Right Plan, the Wrong Clock: How the Iran War Exposed Europe's Air Defense Timeline
item.description: The Iran conflict has turned a theoretical vulnerability into an operational crisis and Europe does not have the time to respond.

item.title: Memory as a Weapon: How Sudan’s April 2023 War Is Fought Through History
item.description: Sudan’s 2023 war is fought not only with weapons, but through competing historical narratives that shape identity, legitimize violence, and undermine prospects for lasting peace.

item.title: Terrorist Innovation Model and Drone Adoption Explained | GNET Insights
item.description: Rueben Dass explains the terrorist innovation model and how groups use drones through adaptation, knowledge transfer, and access to technology.
